transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Cascade, Head of ML), Noah Rivera (Cascade Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Cascade Sec & Compliance)

Auto-generated Summary (may contain errors):
Kickoff for cascade poc, discuss timeline, access, bench, success criteria. Action items captured.

—— Transcript ——
[00:00] Maya Chen: all right good afternoon everyone thanks for hopping on. this is maya from redwood, and with me is liam our solutions eng. how are you all?
[00:08] Asha Patel: hi maya, thanks. excited to get going. we have a fairly aggressive timeline so want to be pragmatic.
[00:13] Noah Rivera: hey team, noah here. we'll cover network constraints, tokenization quirks.
[00:17] Priya Singh: priya — i'll focus on security, honestly we need SOC2 evidence and KMS flow.
[00:22] Liam O'Connor: great, quick agenda: align success criteria, walk through workload sizing, access/onboarding steps, benchmark plan, then milestones — kickoff access, midpoint, exec readout.
[00:31] Maya Chen: quick note, i'll own the commercial SOW and pricing lane, liam will run the bench and tech ops.
[00:36] Asha Patel: sounds good. our internal target: p95 latency under 300ms for single-turn inference at our expected load, quality parity or better than our current hosted vendor on intent detection, and unit cost reduction of about 25%.
[00:50] Liam O'Connor: helpful. for clarity, is that 300ms end-to-end from our application to response or strictly model inference?
[00:55] Asha Patel: end-to-end is ideal, but open to breaking into inference p95 under 200ms and network overhead ~100ms.
[01:04] Maya Chen: noted. on workload: what are you seeing for qps and token lengths?
[01:09] Noah Rivera: current prod steady-state is ~40 qps avg, spikes up to 180 qps for short windows. avg request is 120 total tokens (prompt+response) but we have a heavy long-tail up to 600 tokens for some clinical summaries.
[01:21] Liam O'Connor: okay that's helpful — for the POC we typically test at baseline 50 qps, then step up to 200 qps to validate autoscale and batching behavior. we'll also include long-seq runs to validate kv-cache behavior and memory usage.
[01:36] Priya Singh: on the security side we need to ensure keys never leave our KMS, audit logging at token- or request-level if possible, and SSO via SAML 2.0. any hosted options require separate agreement.
[01:48] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; for hosted we have secure transit and SSE but understand that's sometimes not enough. we'll document the options.
[01:58] Asha Patel: good. can you share the network checklist? our infra team needs the ip ranges, peering steps, and firewall rules.
[02:04] Liam O'Connor: yes i'll share the access playbook. two paths: 1) VPC peering (preferred) with IAM-based temp creds for the pilot, or 2) short-lived API tokens and an ingress VPN for the first-week onboarding.
[02:17] Noah Rivera: peering preferred. we want to avoid public endpoints in prod.
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: noted. for benchmarks — we'll run three passes: baseline (50 qps), stress (200 qps), and quality/regression with your golden prompts. for each pass we'll capture p50/p95/p99, token throughput, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:35] Asha Patel: golden prompts — we have a set of 250 prompts across 3 categories. we'll redact PHI and share an anonymized set.
[02:42] Priya Singh: on redaction — we need an approved process. we'll provide a schema and redaction rules. we cannot expose raw PHI to vendor.
[02:49] Maya Chen: understood. we'll sign an NDA addendum as needed and accept only anonymized payloads.
[02:55] Liam O'Connor: technical detail: when we run the baseline, we'll use a quantized model variant to show a conservative cost/latency baseline and also a fp16 variant to show best-effort latency. caching will be on for prefix-heavy traffic.
[03:09] Asha Patel: what's the expected gap between quantized and fp16?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: typically quantized adds ~10-25% latency but reduces tokens cost by 30-60% depending on model and sequence length. exact numbers will be in the benchmark report.
[03:22] Maya Chen: let's define success gates so everyone is aligned. propose: Gate 1 (kickoff/access complete) — all engineers have network access and sample runs working; Gate 2 (midpoint) — baseline and stress benchmarks complete with p95 inference under 300ms and cost within 30% of target; Gate 3 (exec readout) — quality/regression passes and recommendation for next phase. Does that map to what you expect?
[03:44] Asha Patel: yes though i want a slightly tighter cost target; 25% reduction is our aspirational but we'll accept 30% as POC pass.
[03:50] Priya Singh: plus compliance pass: audit logs and key management validated.
[03:54] Noah Rivera: and we need to validate long-seq behavior to ensure context windows and KV cache don't cause OOMs.
[03:59] Liam O'Connor: we'll include memory profiling and a crash recovery checklist.
[04:05] Maya Chen: timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) — kickoff and access; week 1 — baseline bench and initial tuning; week 2-3 — stress tests and long-seq; week 4 — mid-point review; week 5-6 — regression tests, exec readout prep, final readout on week 6. so roughly a 6-week pilot.
[04:22] Asha Patel: that's tight but acceptable. can we compress if early signals are positive?
[04:26] Maya Chen: yes, we can accelerate the midpoint if all baseline metrics are met early.
[04:29] Liam O'Connor: logistically: i'll need a bastion user or peering details, sample payloads, and the golden prompts. plus a point of contact for network ops.
[04:37] Noah Rivera: i'll be that POC and can get the peering approved, expect a lead time of 3 business days once details are sent.
[04:44] Priya Singh: iam & compliance: we require SOC2 report, encryption in transit and at rest, and attestations for data handling. are those in your standard pack?
[04:54] Maya Chen: yes, we'll share our security packet and SOC2. for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and on-prem options — again we'll share a configuration guide.
[05:04] Asha Patel: for readout to execs we want a one-page summary with topline stats: latency, cost delta, quality regression, and recommended next steps.
[05:12] Maya Chen: we'll deliver that along with the benchmark workbook and raw logs.
[05:16] Liam O'Connor: one more thing — fallback strategy. if the high qps runs show instability, Redwood can route to a smaller variant during spikes to maintain SLA. we can show a canary strategy in the POC.
[05:28] Asha Patel: valuable. also want to flag data residency — some EU data must not cross region boundaries. will that impact the POC?
[05:36] Liam O'Connor: we can run region-specific endpoints for those traffics; for the POC we can constrain tests to a single region which matches your dataset.
[05:44] Priya Singh: ok — please include region and residency notes in the access playbook.
[05:48] Maya Chen: will do.
[05:50] [10:02] Side chatter and brief mute/unmute while Liam pulls up the benchmark template.
[10:25] Liam O'Connor: i'm sharing my screen now — schematic of the benchmark passes and the measurement columns. columns: run id, qps, concurrency, p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, GPU% avg, cost per 1k tokens, notes.
[10:41] Asha Patel: that's perfect. can we add a column for model variant and quantization flag?
[10:46] Liam O'Connor: yes will add model_variant and quant_flag.
[10:49] Noah Rivera: for data — i'll produce a small CSV of token distribution so you can tune batch sizes.
[10:55] Liam O'Connor: ideal. batch sizing will be workload-driven; we won't assume a single batch size.
[11:01] Maya Chen: does anyone have blockers that would prevent access this week?
[11:06] Noah Rivera: firewall change requires security review but should be minor, 3 business days.
[11:11] Priya Singh: need the SOC2 attestation first before peering approval.
[11:15] Maya Chen: we'll send SOC2 and KMS docs by EOD tomorrow.
[11:19] Asha Patel: availability note — exec readout tentatively week of 2026-03-02, two execs need to attend.
[11:27] Maya Chen: we'll pencil that in and confirm after midpoint.
[11:31] Liam O'Connor: timeline recap and acceptance criteria: baseline p95 <= 300ms end-to-end (inference p95 <=200ms), cost delta target -25% (pass if <= -30%), quality regression < 3% false negative increase on intent detection, audit + KMS validated.
[11:46] Asha Patel: that seems clear.
[11:49] Maya Chen: last bit — who will own the exec readout slide pack?
[11:52] Asha Patel: i'll provide a slide with business context, maya will provide technical results.
[11:58] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll compile the one-pager.
[12:01] Liam O'Connor: ok i'll follow up with the benchmark harness and sample scripts plus the network checklist.
[12:06] Maya Chen: terrific. any final questions?
[12:09] Priya Singh: just to confirm we'll only receive anonymized payloads for the initial bench.
[12:13] Liam O'Connor: yes that's our preference and required for the hosted runs.
[12:16] Asha Patel: good. thanks everyone.
[12:19] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll circulate notes and action items. look forward to the kickoff.
[12:23] End of recording.

Notes and links referenced: benchmark_template.xlsx (shared), access_playbook_v1.pdf (to be shared), security_packet_SOC2.zip (to be shared after NDA if required).
